questions.question: What is an astronaut?
answers: A person trained to travel and work in space
A fish that lives in rivers
questions.explanation: Astronauts (and cosmonauts) are people trained to fly and work in space.

questions.question: What do we call the path a satellite takes around Earth?
questions.explanation: An orbit is a curved path around a planet or moon.

questions.question: In 1969, Apollo 11 astronauts walked on the…
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed people on the Moon in 1969.

questions.question: A rocket is useful because it can…
answers: Push itself upward with hot gas thrust
questions.explanation: Rockets expel gas downward to push the vehicle up (Newton’s third law).

questions.question: The first artificial satellite launched into space was named…
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in 1957, the first artificial satellite.

questions.question: Where do many astronauts live and work for months today?
questions.explanation: The ISS is a large laboratory in orbit around Earth where crews live and research.

questions.question: What keeps the Moon going around Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls the Moon toward Earth while its motion keeps it in orbit.

questions.question: A satellite can help people on Earth by…
questions.explanation: Satellites support weather forecasts, GPS-style navigation, TV, and science.

questions.question: Neil Armstrong is famous for…
answers: Being among the first people to walk on the Moon
Painting the first cave art only
questions.explanation: Armstrong was the first person to step onto the lunar surface on Apollo 11.

questions.question: In space, far from a planet’s surface, astronauts float because…
answers: They and their craft are falling around Earth together (microgravity)
There is magic glue on their boots only
The Sun pushes them sideways only
questions.explanation: Orbiting is continuous freefall that creates a feeling of weightlessness.

questions.question: Who was the first human to orbit Earth (1961)?
answers: Wright brothers together in one capsule
questions.explanation: Yuri Gagarin completed one orbit on Vostok 1 in April 1961.

questions.question: What year did Apollo 11 land people on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969 (UTC date conventions may vary by zone).

questions.question: Valentina Tereshkova is famous for…
answers: Being the first woman to fly in space
Drawing the first map of Mars only
questions.explanation: Tereshkova flew on Vostok 6 in 1963, the first woman in space.

questions.question: Why do rockets need multiple stages?
answers: To drop empty tanks and go lighter as they climb
questions.explanation: Staging discards empty mass so remaining engines can accelerate the payload more efficiently.

questions.question: The Hubble Space Telescope is special because it…
answers: Observes space from above most of Earth’s atmosphere
questions.explanation: Hubble’s orbit above much of the atmosphere gives sharper images of deep space.

questions.question: The Space Race of the 1950s–60s was mainly a competition between…
answers: The United States and the Soviet Union
questions.explanation: U.S. and Soviet programs raced for satellite, human, and lunar firsts.

questions.question: What is a rover on Mars?
answers: A robot vehicle that explores the surface
A cloud that rains only candy
questions.explanation: Rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance study Mars geology and climate remotely.

questions.question: GPS-style navigation for phones often depends on…
answers: A constellation of satellites timing signals
Only paper maps glued to shoes
questions.explanation: Global navigation satellite systems broadcast precise time signals receivers use to locate themselves.

questions.question: What was the Space Shuttle designed to do?
answers: Launch like a rocket, land like a glider, and fly to orbit many times
Only map the ocean floor by swimming
questions.explanation: NASA’s Shuttle (1981–2011) carried crews and cargo to orbit and landed on a runway.

questions.question: Low Earth orbit is where…
answers: Many satellites and the ISS travel around Earth relatively close by
The center of the Sun is
The bottom of the deepest mine only
A cave under the Moon only
questions.explanation: LEO is a region of orbits a few hundred kilometers up, used by the ISS and many satellites.

questions.question: John Glenn is known in U.S. space history for…
answers: Being the first American to orbit Earth
Inventing the airplane alone in 1900 only
Discovering Pluto with a phone only
questions.explanation: Glenn orbited Earth in Friendship 7 during Project Mercury.

questions.question: Why do spacesuits protect astronauts on a spacewalk?
answers: They supply air, pressure, and temperature control
They only look shiny for photos
questions.explanation: Suits act like tiny ships: oxygen, pressure, cooling, and micrometeoroid layers.

questions.question: China’s first astronaut (taikonaut) in space was…
questions.explanation: Yang Liwei flew Shenzhou 5 in 2003, China’s first crewed spaceflight.

questions.question: What does “payload” mean on a rocket launch?
answers: The cargo or spacecraft the rocket is carrying
questions.explanation: Payload is the useful mass delivered — satellites, probes, or crewed capsules.

questions.question: The International Space Station is special because…
answers: Many countries built and operate it together
It is permanently on the Moon’s surface only
It is only a movie set
questions.explanation: The ISS is a multinational laboratory continuously crewed since 2000.

questions.question: Sputnik 1’s 1957 launch is historically important because it…
answers: Proved artificial satellites could orbit Earth and opened the Space Age
questions.explanation: Sputnik demonstrated orbital technology and accelerated global space efforts.

questions.question: Project Gemini’s main goal for NASA was to…
answers: Practice rendezvous, docking, and longer flights before Apollo
Only grow corn in orbit for fun
questions.explanation: Gemini developed skills and systems needed for Apollo lunar missions.

questions.question: Apollo used a lunar module so that…
answers: A light lander could touch the Moon while the command ship stayed in lunar orbit
Astronauts could drive underwater cars only
The Sun could be landed on safely
questions.explanation: The LM landed two astronauts; the CSM waited in lunar orbit for return to Earth.

questions.question: Skylab was…
answers: America’s first space station in the 1970s
questions.explanation: Skylab hosted three crewed missions studying Earth, Sun, and long-duration flight.

questions.question: Reusable first-stage boosters (like modern Falcon 9 landings) matter because they…
answers: Can lower launch cost by flying hardware more than once
questions.explanation: Recovering boosters aims to make access to space more affordable and frequent.

questions.question: Crew Dragon (SpaceX) is notable in recent history for…
answers: Carrying astronauts to the ISS under commercial crew contracts
Being the first wooden ship to Mars
questions.explanation: Since 2020, Crew Dragon has regularly flown NASA and other crews to the ISS.

questions.question: NASA’s Artemis program is primarily focused on…
answers: Returning humans to the Moon and preparing for deeper exploration
questions.explanation: Artemis aims for sustainable lunar exploration with international and commercial partners.

questions.question: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) mainly observes in…
answers: Infrared light to study early galaxies and star formation
questions.explanation: JWST’s infrared instruments look through dust and back in cosmic time.

questions.question: Escape velocity is best described as…
answers: The speed needed to break free of a body’s gravitational pull without further thrust
The speed of sound only on Earth always
A speed that removes mass from Earth
questions.explanation: Escape velocity depends on mass and radius of the body you are leaving.

questions.question: The first soft landing of a probe on Mars that returned useful surface data included missions such as…
questions.explanation: Viking 1 and 2 landed in 1976 and returned landmark Mars surface science.

questions.question: A geostationary satellite appears nearly fixed in the sky because it…
answers: Orbits once per day above the equator matching Earth’s rotation
questions.explanation: GEO altitude and equatorial placement keep the satellite over one longitude.

questions.question: Sally Ride is remembered as…
answers: The first American woman in space (1983, STS-7)
The inventor of the steam engine only
The first person on Mars in 1950
questions.explanation: Ride flew on the Space Shuttle Challenger on STS-7 in 1983.

questions.question: Tiangong is…
answers: China’s modular space station in low Earth orbit
A type of desert cactus only
questions.explanation: China’s Tiangong station hosts crews and research in LEO.

questions.question: Why is re-entry heating a big engineering problem?
answers: Air compresses and heats the craft as it slams into the atmosphere at high speed
Space is full of lava fountains always
There is no air friction ever
questions.explanation: Heat shields manage extreme temperatures during atmospheric re-entry.

questions.question: Voyager 1 is famous partly because it…
answers: Flew past outer planets and later entered interstellar space
questions.explanation: Voyager 1 explored the outer solar system and crossed into interstellar space.

questions.question: CubeSats are important today because they…
answers: Let universities and small teams fly small, cheaper satellites
questions.explanation: Standardized small satellites lowered the barrier to flying experiments.

questions.question: Private companies launching astronauts in the 2020s shows that…
answers: Commercial partners now share crewed access to orbit with government agencies
questions.explanation: Commercial crew and tourism flights expanded who can fly and how missions are bought.

questions.question: A transfer orbit (like Hohmann) is used mainly to…
answers: Move a spacecraft between two circular orbits efficiently
questions.explanation: Hohmann transfers use timed burns to change orbital energy with less propellant.

questions.question: The first soft landing on the Moon’s far side was achieved by…
answers: Only Apollo 11 on the near side again
questions.explanation: Chang’e-4 landed in Von Kármán crater on the lunar far side in 2019.

questions.question: Starlink and similar mega-constellations mainly provide…
answers: Broadband internet via many satellites in low Earth orbit
questions.explanation: Large LEO constellations aim for global connectivity; they also raise space-traffic concerns.

questions.question: Apollo–Soyuz (1975) is remembered as…
answers: A docking of U.S. and Soviet spacecraft symbol symbol Cold War cooperation
questions.explanation: Apollo–Soyuz Test Project practiced joint docking and showed political thaw in space.

questions.question: Why do astronauts exercise on the ISS?
answers: To reduce bone and muscle loss in microgravity
Because space has heavier gravity than Earth always
To make the station spin faster only
Exercise is banned on Earth only
questions.explanation: Without loading, bones and muscles weaken; exercise counters some effects.

questions.question: Ingenuity on Mars was special as…
answers: The first powered aircraft to fly on another planet
The first wooden ship on Earth
A subway train under Paris only
questions.explanation: NASA’s Ingenuity helicopter proved controlled flight in Mars’s thin atmosphere.

questions.question: Ion thrusters are useful in deep space because they…
answers: Provide efficient low-thrust propulsion over long times using electric power
questions.explanation: Electric propulsion trades low thrust for high efficiency on long missions.

questions.question: From Sputnik (1957) to today, the biggest change in human spaceflight access is…
answers: More nations and commercial companies can launch and operate spacecraft
Only one country may use radio
questions.explanation: Space activity broadened from two superpowers to many agencies and companies worldwide.

questions.question: A rocket countdown goes 3, 2, 1… What number comes just before liftoff after 1?
questions.explanation: Countdowns reach zero at liftoff.

questions.question: If a satellite completes 16 orbits in one day, about how many hours is one orbit?
questions.explanation: 24 hours / 16 orbits ≈ 1.5 hours per orbit (ISS is near this range).

questions.question: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. If a radio signal travels at light speed, a one-way message to a probe near Mars at a time when Mars is 12 light-minutes away takes about…
questions.explanation: Signals cannot beat light speed; delay equals distance in light-time.

questions.question: True or false reasoning: All rockets need fuel. This vehicle is a rocket. Therefore…
questions.explanation: If all rockets need fuel and this is a rocket, it needs fuel.

questions.question: Launches near the equator can get a free speed boost eastward because…
answers: Earth rotates fastest there, helping rockets going east
questions.explanation: Earth’s rotation gives an eastward velocity; larger near the equator.

questions.question: The word “lunar” is about the…
questions.explanation: Lunar means related to the Moon.

questions.question: “Microgravity” means…
answers: A condition of very small apparent weight, as in freefall orbit
questions.explanation: Microgravity describes the near-weightless freefall environment of orbit.

questions.question: Many space posters show Earth as a blue marble. Blue mainly shows…
questions.explanation: Oceans and sky tones make Earth look blue from space.

questions.question: Mission Control is a place where teams…
answers: Watch spacecraft data and help astronauts
questions.explanation: Flight controllers monitor systems and communicate with the crew.

questions.question: People first launched a satellite before people first…
questions.explanation: Sputnik (1957) came before Apollo 11 (1969).
